gloss: popular; commonplace; easy to understand; vulgar

definitions.gloss: popular; commonplace; accessible; easy to understand
definitions.explanation: Aimed at or understandable by ordinary people rather than specialists. Can carry either a neutral tone (accessible) or a slightly negative connotation (lowbrow, unsophisticated).

examples.japanese: {通俗|つうぞく}{的|てき}な{表現|ひょうげん}を{使|つか}う。
{通俗|つうぞく}{小説|しょうせつ}は{広|ひろ}い{読者層|どくしゃそう}に{支持|しじ}されている。
examples.english: Popular novels are supported by a wide readership.

examples.japanese: {専門的|せんもんてき}な{内容|ないよう}を{通俗|つうぞく}{的|てき}にわかりやすく{説明|せつめい}するのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It is difficult to explain specialized content in an accessible, easy-to-understand way.

notes:
Describes something aimed at the general public rather than experts or the elite. Depending on context, it can be neutral (accessible, easy to understand) or slightly negative (lowbrow, lacking sophistication). Often used as a modifier with {的|てき}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {通俗|つうぞく}{的|てき}: popular; commonplace (adjectival)
- {通俗|つうぞく}{小説|しょうせつ}: popular fiction
- {通俗|つうぞく}{科学|かがく}: popular science
- {通俗|つうぞく}{的|てき}な{解釈|かいしゃく}: a popular (simplified) interpretation

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {大衆|たいしゅう}{的|てき}: popular / mass-market — focuses on appeal to the masses
- {俗|ぞく}: vulgar / common — more negative; emphasizes crudeness
- {平易|へいい}な: plain / easy to understand — purely about simplicity, no negative connotation

REGISTER:
Formal and somewhat literary. Used in academic, literary criticism, and media contexts.
